statement: A bridgeless cubic graph that contains a triangle can always be 3-edge-colored (the triangle can be contracted and any 3-edge-coloring lifted back).
definitions: Graphs are finite and simple; cubic = 3-regular; bridgeless = no edge whose removal disconnects the graph; a 3-edge-colouring assigns edges 3 colours with adjacent edges coloured differently.
ground_truth_witness: Tietze's graph on vertices 0..11 with the 18 edges 0-1 0-5 0-9 1-2 1-6 2-3 2-7 3-8 3-10 4-6 4-7 4-11 5-7 5-8 6-8 9-10 9-11 10-11, obtained from the Petersen graph by replacing one vertex with a triangle. It is 3-regular, bridgeless, and contains the triangle 9-10-11, yet exhaustive search shows its edges cannot be properly 3-colored; its chromatic index is 4. (Contracting the triangle gives back the Petersen graph, which is itself not 3-edge-colorable, so the lifting step has nothing to lift.)
reference_authority: online-cited counterexample (MO/MSE/CS.SE/Wikipedia) with verify script, verified per partB_feasibility records
